summary: Reviewed the committed T2 implementation (backend/src/ics_import.rs, the lib.rs module export, and the three ics_import_service tests) against the T2 acceptance criteria and the approved ics-import design; found no concrete defects and the three service tests pass.
follow_up: 00-status.md marks T3 'waiting' but the T3 HTTP endpoint (import_ics handler, /api/v1/calendars/:calendar_id/import-ics route, map_ics_import_error) is already committed in HEAD — reconcile the status doc.

max_components is set to max_events + 100 (1100) and counts ALL BEGIN components including VALARM, so a valid calendar with many alarms can trip LimitExceeded; document this as an intentional design choice.
Empty SUMMARY is parser-allowed but rejected by validate_mutation (non-empty title required), mapping to InvalidCalendar (400); defensible but worth documenting.
important_context: T2 code is committed (f8c39b9); the only backend working-tree changes are T1's (event.rs record_caldav_change in create_batch + caldav test assertions), not T2's.

IcsImportService::import enforces MAX_ICS_IMPORT_BYTES (1 MiB) at the service level and uses MAX_ICS_IMPORT_EVENTS (1,000) with max_components 1,100; map_parse_error maps LimitExceeded->LimitExceeded and all other parser codes->InvalidCalendar; map_service_error maps NotFound->NotFound, Database->Database, else->InvalidCalendar.

convert_calendar rejects detached-on-non-recurring-master, duplicate exception keys per master, overrides carrying rrule/exdates, key-kind mismatch vs master timing, orphan detached instances, and empty calendars before delegating once to create_batch.
Parser status validation is case-sensitive (uppercase CONFIRMED/TENTATIVE/CANCELLED only) — a parser defect outside T2 scope, not reported as a T2 defect.
